role_reviews.finding: This calibration attempt is worse than the preceding failed batch: it turns nine game screenshots into a blue-sky field. The tiny floating wrist tool becomes the only object and is an immediate prototype signal.
The route cannot be read at all. Six late frames miss their requested authored region and no later gameplay can be evaluated.

The alignment control used an inverted Three.js pitch convention and then clamped virtual mouse movement, causing an unrecoverable near-vertical view. Recorded camera direction Y≈+0.9468 is decisive runtime evidence.
Positive camera-rig X rotation is upward in this scene. Correct the default to a small negative pitch and drive probe alignment from `asin(direction.y)` using unbounded relative mouse movement only.
Reject all nine images. This is zero usable visual evidence; screenshots show sky and a detached black wrist shape, not a game world.

required_fix: Correct the pitch sign and remove virtual-pointer edge clamping. Capture a fresh Dispatch-only calibration batch first, inspect its measured camera directions and visible lower route before attempting later-region traversal again.
approval_rule: CAPTURED is true and INSPECTED is true. APPROVED is false. Scores remain null because sky-only technical-invalid screenshots must not receive fabricated artistic grades.
